Code review clean. Resolve the merge conflict before merge. Label: `conflicts`.

This is a safety-tier review because the change affects posted G-code.

- Fanuc, Doosan and Mazak refuse a positive G83 dwell by name. Their zero-dwell cycles still work.
- Haas includes dwell in the cycle signature and writes P0 to clear the previous dwell.
- The tests cover the refusals, milliseconds, dwell changes and zero reset. The decision file records the control limits.
- No UI files changed. Screenshots are not required.

Local build and tests

The trial merge with `upstream/main` at `17a8c6e7608bb7078f75ec335361839712e51425` failed in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_haas.nc:37`. Main adds decimal points. This PR adds P0. I aborted the merge, as the review rules require, and tested the unchanged PR head. These results do not verify the combined tree. No GitHub runner was used.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`: passed; plan only.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 528 passed, zero failed.
- App library: 313 passed, one ignored.
- App `bore_cycle`: 3 passed; `commands_undo`: 30 passed; `conformance`: 7 passed; `mcp`: 22 passed.
- App `operations`: 119 passed, six ignored.
- App `post_cycle_feed_spindle`: 8 passed; `ream_cycle`: 3 passed; `recorded_post_streams`: 5 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

Mutation checks

I ran both mutations separately in the review worktree and restored the file after each check.

1. Remove dwell from the Haas G83 signature. `haas_g83_updates_dwell_in_an_open_cycle_group` failed: one G83 block instead of two. Restore the line: passed.
2. Remove unconditional P output for Haas G83. `haas_g83_zero_dwell_clears_modal_p` failed: the second G83 block had no P0. Restore the condition: passed.

Goldens and sources

I checked all seven added or changed golden files line by line. Six bore files come from parent PR #1821. This PR adds only P0 to the G83 line in `synth_haas.nc`. The tests reproduce these files. The [Haas G83 reference](https://legacy-aem.haascnc.com/content/haascnc/en/service/codes-settings.type=gcode.machine=mill.value=G83.html) documents reuse of dwell. The [Haas G04 reference](https://legacy-aem.haascnc.com/content/haascnc/en/service/codes-settings.type=gcode.machine=mill.value=G04.html) documents modal P and integer milliseconds.

Requested code changes: none.

At merge time, refresh after parent #1821. Keep main's decimal formatting and this PR's P0 in the conflicting golden. Run the relevant tests on that result. No real control was tested. The full quick, batch and release gates were not run in this review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Independent safety-floor review (pre-cut). This review does not use the conclusions of earlier markers on this PR.

### What looks good
- Fanuc, Mazak and Doosan DNM refuse a positive G83 dwell by name. The refusal comes before `xyFirst` and `cycleSeat`, so no move and no G83 block is written (`assets/posts/fanuc.cps:1064`, `mazak.cps:890`, `doosan-dnm.cps:1226`).
- Haas writes P as integer milliseconds (`ms = Math.round(p.P * 1000)`, P in the stream is seconds). This agrees with the Haas G04/G83 convention for a P without a decimal point.
- Haas puts the dwell into the G83 cycle signature (`haas.cps:904`) and always writes P on G83, P0 included (`haas.cps:917`). A changed dwell restarts the cycle, and a zero dwell clears the modal P.
- Negative or non-finite dwell cannot reach the post: `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:22` refuses it. So `P-500` or `PNaN` on Haas G83 is not possible.
- Each branch has a pin in `crates/post/tests/g83_dwell.rs`: three refusals (0.001 s and 0.5 s), zero dwell on all four posts, Haas P500, Haas dwell change (P500 then P750), Haas P0 reset.
- The test file is in the lowest crate (`camcraft-post`), and its Gate map names `camcraft_post::post::engine`. `expect` is only in test code.
- The decision record `docs/decisions/1820-g83-dwell.md` cites public manuals. It states the Doosan and Mazak limits honestly. No third-party post text is copied.
- The golden change is one word (`P0` in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_haas.nc`), and the PR body explains it.
- No snapshot PNG, no process file, no dependency, no `build.rs`. The stacked parent #1821 is merged.

### Results, merged with main (locally, Windows 11)
Head `12e68529f` trial-merged with `origin/main` `1db03daa6`: no conflicts.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-post` all test binaries (lib, bin and 73 test files) | pass, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-post --test g83_dwell` | 7 passed |
| `camcraft-post --test script_haas` / `script_fanuc` / `script_mazak` / `script_doosan_dnm` | 11 / 11 / 11 / 11 passed |
| `camcraft-post --test doosan_dnm_post` / `fanuc_post` / `bore_cycle` / `cycle_hop` | 9 / 12 / 7 / 7 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test conformance` (synth goldens, `synth_haas.nc` included) | 7 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test post_cycle_feed_spindle` / `program_units` / `control_comp` / `wear_comp` | 8 / 7 / 5 / 5 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The goldens give the same output on Windows. I found no platform-dependent output. `camcraft-app` source does not change, so I did not run clippy on it.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. Other posts have the same class of problem, outside the scope of #1820 (Fanuc family). `assets/posts/grblhal.cps:725` and `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1094` write P only on G82/G86/G89. A G83 dwell on these posts is dropped and no message is given. `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:725` writes `P<ms>` on G83 in ISO mode, and this is not verified for that control. I recommend a `source:agent` follow-up issue for these three posts.
2. The Haas signature fix applies only to G83. On G82 and G89 the signature is still `g|Z|R|Q`. Two back-to-back holes with a different dwell in one open cycle group keep the first P. This is the same modal problem, and it existed before this PR. It can go into the same follow-up issue.
3. The refusal text prints `p.P` directly (for example `0.001 s`). The G86 refusal prints `ms / 1000`. The two texts are both correct; the format is only slightly different.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
